title: ML routing + fallback lab scribbles
content:
Quick brain-dump from the eu-west1 flakey-routing runs. Not polished — steps, things tried, raw outputs and some theories. Use this as a running notebook; I will split into a proper write-up later.

Incident summary (short):
- Observed repeated small-window double-ejects where a single request causes two sequential fallback executions (primary -> fallback-A -> fallback-B) and the client sees two abrupt truncations. Only in eu-west1 region; others normal.
- Triggered during medium burst (~200-600 RPS) for model: redwood/open-13b-quant-causal at seq=1024.
- First noticed 2026-02-16 09:12 UTC during synthetic canary traffic.

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
- stale smart-routing policy cached on edge nodes (TTL mismatch between control-plane and router nodes) -> a newly-rolled policy is half-applied, causing route election flip mid-request.
- KV cache (prefix/KV) warm-up race: one router returns a cached prefix but KV-cache miss causes fallback to a lower-capacity variant, which in turn triggers a fallback policy leading to secondary fallback.
- clock skew / leader election: distributed routing table reconciliation takes >50ms in eu-west1 under load, causing transient policy divergence between machines in same AZ.
- hidden transform in the routing policy `allow-multi-fallback: true` combined with `eject-on-latency=200ms` causing an eager secondary-eject.

Commands I ran (raw):
- curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer xXx' 'https://api.eu-west1.redwood.ai/v1/route/inspect?route=smart-router-req'
  -> shows policy version 2026-02-16_08:58:12 on node-a, 2026-02-15_22:01:08 on node-b (BAD)

- kubectl -n serving logs router-pod-7 --since=15m | grep -E "eject|fallback|policy" --color=never
  -> repeated lines: "policy-snapshot mismatch: local=v32 control=v33" and "eject: policy-route mismatch, fallback_count=1"

- grpcurl -plaintext router-service:9000 RouteService.GetDebugTable | jq '.routes[] | select(.name=="smart-router-req")'
  -> node responses disagree on `max_family_fallbacks` value (2 vs 1)

- redis-cli -h redis-eu-west1 dump route:snapshots:smart-router-req-2026-02-16
  -> dump shows two entries with timestamps 08:58:12 and 22:01:08 (control-plane rolled twice?)

- python snippets to compare snapshots (saved as /tmp/snapshots-compare-20260218.txt)

Raw log snippets (copied verbatim):
[2026-02-16T09:12:10.412Z] router-pod-7 [INFO] route-evaluated id=abc123 latency=189ms -> choose=variant-A
[2026-02-16T09:12:10.621Z] router-pod-7 [WARN] fallback-triggered id=abc123 cause=kv-miss fallback=variant-B
[2026-02-16T09:12:10.622Z] router-pod-8 [INFO] route-evaluated id=abc123 latency=210ms -> choose=variant-B (different policy version)
[2026-02-16T09:12:10.623Z] router-pod-7 [ERROR] double-eject detected for id=abc123 trace=trace-zzz

What I tried and notes: 
- Force-apply policy with sequence bump (control-plane): `curl -X POST /admin/policies/activate?force=true` -> immediate rollout visible on new pod logs but older nodes still report v32 for ~12s. That's longer than expected TTL of 2s. Suspect we have a *staggered* apply process which is not pushing invalidation to router caches.
- Flushed redis keys for the route snapshots. Observed spike in kgens as routers rebuild their local caches; during rebuild window, double-eject rate increased. That suggests KV-cache rebuild itself is risky.
- Deployed temporary config to set `max_family_fallbacks=1` everywhere via a canary rollout (patch in PR #862). Canary nodes applied quickly, but the control-plane then fell back to the older snapshot because a reconciler check failed in 1 node due to a validation rule. Need to track that validator.
- Restarted routers in a controlled AZ; double-ejects dropped for ~90s then resumed. Restart helps but is not a root fix.

Measurements / observations: 
- Double-ejects correlate strongly with periods of control-plane policy churn (deploys) + RPS bursts.
- Only in eu-west1 (nodes: router-pod-5..9). Other regions had identical canary traffic but stable.
- Heap/CPU on router pods looked fine (no OOM), but p90 GC spikes coincident with config reloads.

To-dos / experiments next: 
- Add an explicit cache-invalidation RPC: control-plane should call `router:invalidate(policy_id)` on every router after activate. Check whether such a call failed in the logs around 08:58.
- Reproduce locally: run 3 router instances, inject a TTL mismatch and simulate 500 RPS with our existing canary harness; attempt to provoke double-ejects.
- Add telemetry: emit both control-policy-version + local-policy-version in each router response header (fast to add) so we can easily correlate client traces to mis-match events.
- Short-term mitigation: set routers to drop-instead-of-double-eject when policy mismatch is detected (i.e., prefer single fallback and log) — quick patch in runtime.
- Audit the validator that prevented canary from fully applying the `max_family_fallbacks=1` config; possibly too strict and causing partial rollbacks.

Notes on root-cause suspicion: 
- My current strongest hunch is race between policy apply + KV cache rebuild. Control-plane applies a new routing policy; it writes snapshots to redis, but some routers refresh their policy by reading from redis while others use a local in-memory copy until TTL expiry. If the redis snapshot contains a slightly different `fallback_family` ordering (due to an earlier transient merge), requests flowing through different routers during the merge window can get inconsistent fallback decisions. When a router with older policy receives a request already rerouted by a different router (proxy chain), the resulting mismatch shows up as double-ejects.

Quick checklist for next on-call run: 
- [ ] Check policy apply logs around incident time (control-plane, timestamp 08:55-09:15) for invalidation RPCs.
- [ ] Confirm whether the controller sends an explicit invalidate message (search logs for 'invalidate' RPC).
- [ ] Dump redis keys and check for overlapping snapshot IDs.
- [ ] Re-run canary with `--stagger=0` (attempt atomically apply) if possible.
- [ ] Add instrumentation to trace request IDs across routers (enable trace propagation on canary clients).

Random TODOs (follow-ups):
- Create a small integration test that simulates policy rollouts and checks for consistency across 5 simulated routers. Track this as INFRA-2163.
- PR note: in #862 I added a safety validator; maybe too restrictive. Revisit validation logic with Rajan.

References / breadcrumbs:
- INFRA-2147 (incident ticket) - initial alert + graphs
- PR #862 - canary to limit family fallbacks to 1
- Slack thread: slack:/C03FFX9/thread-incident-eu-west1 (contains heap dumps + pprof links)

If anyone else picks this up: start with control-plane logs + redis snapshots. Prioritize reproducing with a 3-node local setup and the canary harness — reproduction will point at race or config validator.

-- Maya
